subject: Post-demo: control-plane & network isolation — next test plan
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Patel <anya@valorafin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: control-plane & network isolation — next test plan

Hi Anya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary from call:
- ValoraFin is evaluating private/on-prem inference for sensitive payments data; primary asks are control-plane isolation, no outbound egress from GPU hosts, and an auditable handshake for model updates.
- You ran a quick comparison vs a hyperscaler-managed inference endpoint last month and want to validate control-plane separation and air-gap feasibility.

Proposed next tests (we can run these in a sandbox VPC you provide or over a short lived lab environment we manage):
1) Control-plane handshake trace: capture the TLS connection sequence for model checkout (we’ll provide a stubbed client). Expected outcome: show whether control-plane calls can be routed through a customer-controlled NAT/proxy only.
2) Data-plane-only flow: confirm GPUs never initiate outbound flows except to a pre-approved NTP/time service.
3) Offline model activation: simulate model update via signed artifact drop (no inbound pull from central control plane).
4) Network topology validation: we’ll review your topology diagram and call out any routing paths that would allow unexpected egress.

Attached: finsecure_requirements.xlsx (requirements workbook) and a short redwood_test_plan.pdf draft.

Can you: 
- Share your network topology (FW rules, NAT/Proxy endpoints) — a PNG or exported diagram works.
- Confirm whether the lab will be inside your AWS account or if you'd prefer Redwood to spin a temporary VPC for the exercise.
- Propose two 2-hour windows next week for the test run.

We’ll keep the initial test scoped to 2 hours and capture logs we can share with your security team. Happy to redline plan if you have internal constraints.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai

Attachments: finsecure_requirements.xlsx (xlsx), redwood_test_plan.pdf (pdf)
From: Anya Patel <anya@valorafin.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-platform@hyperscalecorp.com
Date: 2027-04-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: control-plane & network isolation — next test plan\n
Thanks Priyom — appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers inline.

> Can you share your network topology?
Attached: valorafin_topology.png — this is our current production-similar topology (sanitized). Key notes: we use a centralized NAT egress via Transit Gateway, strict egress rules, and an internal jump-host for admin ops.

We evaluated a hyperscaler-managed endpoint earlier (summary): model updates were automatic and outbound from the managed host to the provider's control plane. Our security team flagged the lack of an explicit offline activation path and the control-plane telemetry going through the provider's network.

Questions for Redwood before we schedule: 
- How does Redwood’s control plane packet flow look for Private deployments? Can you produce a diagram showing the control-plane endpoints and possible IP ranges?
- For air-gap: can we accept signed model artifacts and have Redwood perform activation without the GPU hosts reaching out?

We can host the lab inside our AWS account — I’ll loop infra and procurement for scheduling, and attach the topology now.

—Anya
CTO, ValoraFin

Attachment: valorafin_topology.png (png)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-23T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo: control-plane & network isolation — next test plan

Folks — quick internal note to align on what to show ValoraFin. I recommend we keep the first lab tight and focused on three repeatable artifacts we can hand them: 

1) Control-plane call trace (pcap + annotated timeline) — show TLS endpoints and who initiated connection. Hyperscaler issue: most managed endpoints show APIServer->provider pulls; we should highlight that Redwood Private can be configured to require customer-provided proxy endpoints.
2) Signed artifact activation demo — run small model activation where the model artifact is uploaded to an S3-like store and the activation is triggered by an operator with a signed token. This demonstrates no outbound pull from GPU nodes.
3) Network egress verification checklist — simple connectivity probes from GPU host to blocked endpoints (we’ll script this).

Operational asks from our side: 
- Ben: prepare the activation script and a signed-artifact flow (can be a simple HMAC-signed JSON token).
- Priyom: confirm whether Valora wants the lab in their AWS account (my preference is inside their account for transparency).
- I’ll draft a short security summary we can share post-test.

Also — we should prep a plain-language comparison document for Anya that contrasts the control-plane behaviors: 
- Hyperscaler-managed endpoints: control-plane out-of-customer network by default; automated model lifecycle; fewer knobs for egress.
- Redwood Private: optional customer-controlled control-plane, signed-artifact activation, audit logs by default (we can provide log export).

I’ll attach a skeleton redwood_test_plan.pdf and we should iterate before sharing.

-Marissa
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_test_plan.pdf (pdf)

Anya — thanks for the topology. We propose these concrete windows for a 2-hour lab (we'll keep it lean):
- Tue 2027-04-27 09:00-11:00 PT
- Wed 2027-04-28 13:00-15:00 PT

Plan we will execute (90-minute run + 30-minute review):
A) Validate control-plane handshake: we will run the client stub to exercise model checkout and capture packets. Deliverable: annotated pcap + timeline.
B) Offline activation: Ben will walk through the signed-artifact activation. Deliverable: activation runbook + audit log snippet.
C) Egress checks: small script that attempts connections to a list of disallowed hosts — deliverable: egress report.

We’ll use the HubSpot ticket HS-40928 to track artifacts — I’ve added the proposed schedule there. Link: HubSpot:HS-40928.

If you confirm Tue or Wed, we’ll send a short infra playbook with the minimal IAM and SG rules we need. Also attaching a slightly updated redwood_test_plan.pdf (minor edits from Marissa).

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

Priyom
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
